title: Finite affine refinement of an atlas of a quasi-compact algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact, meaning that it admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For every representable surjective etale map $w:W\to X$ from a scheme $W$, there are an integer $n\geq0$ and affine open subschemes $W_1,\ldots,W_n\subseteq W$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that their composites $W_i\to X$ are jointly surjective and the induced morphism $p:U=\coprod_{i=1}^nW_i\to X$ is representable surjective etale. The scheme $U$ is affine; if $W_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, then $U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{i=1}^n A_i)$. The empty family is permitted when $X=\varnothing$, with $U=\operatorname{Spec}0$. In particular every quasi-compact algebraic space admits a representable surjective etale morphism from one affine scheme. No quasi-compactness of the specified atlas $W$ and no separatedness assumption are required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-finite-affine-image-selection] to obtain the finite affine opens, their field-extension joint surjectivity, and the empty-atlas cardinality condition. This is exactly the original compactness and finite-subcover portion of the argument.

proof.text: Let F_i be the selected open schemes. Form their scheme coproduct, put d=Sigma.desc of the inclusions into W, and give U its S-map d followed by the map W -> S. Lift the coprojections and d to Over S. Sigma.ι_desc proves the required triangles; the same triangles transfer joint surjectivity from Step 1. The coproduct colimit witness is Cofan.isColimitOfIsIsoSigmaDesc. The scheme map d is etale by IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc, because each summand inclusion is an open immersion. On a scheme test the Yoneda map of d is represented by the scheme pullback; stability of etaleness under base change makes it representably etale. Compose with w using isEtale_comp, whose proof pastes scheme-test pullback squares.

source.place: Tags 03E4 and 03H6, finite affine image subcover of a specified scheme atlas; original refinement proof Steps 1-2.

proof.text: For any test t:h_T -> X, use [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] to obtain its scheme fibre product P with U. For x in T take its residue-field section. Joint surjectivity gives a field extension and a section into one selected summand, hence into U, agreeing with t after extension. The corresponding point of Spec L lies over x by fromSpecResidueField_apply. The final clause of the cited fibre-product theorem makes P -> T surjective. Its flipped square is the scheme-test witness of IsSurjective. This argument uses no further unproved point-surjectivity criterion.

source.place: Tag 03H5, surjectivity by field-valued lifts; scheme-fibre-product point calculation of Tag 03H4.

proof.text: Each selected affine open is an affine scheme. The finite scheme coproduct is affine by Mathlib. Given isomorphisms F_i ≅ Spec A_i, use Sigma.mapIso. Reindex the coproduct by ULift(Fin n), apply asIso(sigmaSpec R) from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], and apply Spec to the product-ring reindexing isomorphism to return to the product over Fin n. If n=0 the coproduct is a colimit of an empty diagram; isColimitEquivIsInitialOfIsEmpty and specPUnitIsInitial identify it with Spec PUnit. Finally apply the refinement to Q -> X from the quasi-compactness hypothesis and retain its affine, etale and surjective conclusions.

The worker's source-error note is correct: 03H6's last sentence says 'finite surjective', which should read étale surjective, and their D(t)⊔D(t−1)→A¹ counterexample checks out. The item statement is unchanged and true. Step 1: |q| is continuous (by the final topology, or by lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus) and surjective (by that lemma's surjectivity criterion), and the 04Z9 leaf then makes |X| qc. Step 2: V_a→X is representable étale by the open-immersion base-change leaf plus clauses (1)–(2) of etale-composition-cancellation; the point images are open by point-open-calculus and cover |X| through |w|, so a finite subcover exists; this is joint surjectivity exactly as def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family defines it. No intersection of affines is used. Step 3: the scheme coproduct leaf gives U; E=U×_W W_T represents h_U×_X h_T (the step writes out the universal-property calculation); E is covered by open E_i whose maps to T are étale; etale-local-on-source (arbitrary cover, empty cover included) gives E→T étale. Step 4: surjectivity follows from the point-image criterion, and U≅Spec∏A_i from the finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum leaf, which has no nonempty hypothesis. Step 5 (elementary) is the X=∅/Spec 0 case and W=Q. Edge cases checked: X empty, infinite non-qc W, doubled-origin W, n=1. Duplicate candidates are lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas (needs an atlas already given as a disjoint union of affines), lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas (existence clause only) and lem-a1-space-etale-open-image; none states the prescribed-atlas refinement. lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_affine_atlas_refinement {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hqc : ∃ (Q : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj Q ⟶ X.obj.obj), CompactSpace Q.left ∧ IsEtale q ∧ IsSurjective q) (W : Over S) (w : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hw : IsEtale w) (hs : IsSurjective w) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (V : Fin n → W.left.Opens) (U : Over S) (j : ∀ i : Fin n, Over.mk ((V i).ι ≫ W.hom) ⟶ U) (a : U ⟶ W), (∀ i : Fin n, IsAffineOpen (V i)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk U.left (fun i : Fin n ↦ (j i).left))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, j i ≫ a = Over.homMk (V := W) (V i).ι rfl) ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun i : Fin n ↦ yoneda.map (j i ≫ a) ≫ w) ∧ IsEtale (yoneda.map a ≫ w) ∧ IsSurjective (yoneda.map a ≫ w) ∧ IsAffine U.left ∧ (∀ (A : Fin n → CommRingCat.{u}), (∀ i : Fin n, Nonempty ((V i).toScheme ≅ Spec (A i))) → Nonempty (U.left ≅ Spec (.of (∀ i : Fin n, A i)))) ∧ (IsEmpty W.left → n = 0) ∧ (n = 0 → Nonempty (U.left ≅ Spec (.of PUnit.{u + 1})))
lean.note: The main theorem states the specified-atlas finite affine refinement, its coproduct and spectrum formula, and its empty case. The second theorem states the final affine-atlas existence clause. The scheme coproduct is expressed by IsColimit and the induced map by its commuting triangles.
